reference_frame.description: Longitudinal positions (x) are metres aft of the forward perpendicular; heights (z) are metres above the top of keel; transverse positions (y) are metres from the centre line, positive to starboard. The forward perpendicular meets the stem at the level of E deck; the after perpendicular is the forward side of the rudder post, 850 ft (259.08 m) aft.
reference_frame.note: Definition of the perpendiculars from the Harland and Wolff sheer plan as described by Halpern. The compartment lengths of the British report add up to exactly 850 ft.

particulars.title: Length overall
particulars.summary: 882 ft 9 in from stem to stern.
particulars.note: Universally quoted figure; Delgado writes of the ship's 882-foot length. Not stated in the report sections read.

particulars.title: Length between perpendiculars
particulars.note: Used in the Harland and Wolff calculations; equal to the sum of the sixteen compartment lengths.

particulars.title: Extreme breadth
particulars.note: Registered breadth 92.5 ft.

particulars.title: Depth, keel to C deck
particulars.summary: 64 ft 9 in from the top of keel to the top of beam at the lowest point of sheer of C deck.
particulars.note: Wikipedia gives 64 ft 6 in; the report is the primary source.

particulars.title: Load draught
particulars.note: Wilding, British Inquiry, Q19796.

particulars.title: Displacement at load draught
particulars.note: Wilding, British Inquiry, Q19797–19798. Converted at 1.01605 t per long ton.

particulars.title: Displacement at the time of the collision
particulars.note: Halpern: load displacement less 28 in of draught at 143.8 long tons per inch of immersion.

particulars.title: Gross register tonnage
particulars.note: A measure of enclosed volume, not of weight.

particulars.title: Speed at the time of the collision
particulars.note: Boxhall's estimate (Q15645) accepted by the report; figures of 22 and 22½ knots were put to Wilding.

particulars.title: Block coefficient
particulars.note: From the Harland and Wolff record of particulars for hull 401, as reported by Halpern.

particulars.title: Prismatic coefficient
particulars.note: Same record.

particulars.title: Midship section coefficient
particulars.summary: About 0.970: a midship section very close to rectangular.
particulars.note: Ratio of the block coefficient to the prismatic coefficient.

particulars.title: Stem head forward of the forward perpendicular
particulars.summary: About 2 ft 6 in at forecastle level; the stem rakes 1 ft in 12 ft.
particulars.note: Derived from the stem rake and the height of the forecastle above the perpendicular's intersection with the stem at E deck.

particulars.title: Stern abaft the after perpendicular
particulars.note: Length overall less the length between perpendiculars and the stem overhang.

particulars.title: Boat deck above keel
particulars.summary: About 92 ft 6 in at the lowest point of sheer; about 60 ft 6 in above the waterline at the time of the accident.
particulars.note: Report, Decks and Accommodation; Wilding, Q19839.

particulars.title: Crow's nest above keel
particulars.summary: A steel look-out cage on the foremast about 95 ft above the load waterline.
particulars.note: The height above the waterline is from the report; the height above keel adds the load draught.

particulars.title: Wing propellers
particulars.summary: Two three-bladed wing propellers, 23 ft 6 in in diameter.
particulars.note: Commonly quoted figure, read in a tertiary source only.

particulars.title: Centre propeller
particulars.summary: One centre propeller driven by the turbine, about 17 ft in diameter.
particulars.note: No photograph of Titanic's centre propeller is known.

alternatives.holder: Older view, by analogy with Olympic

particulars.title: Rudder
particulars.summary: 78 ft 8 in high and 15 ft 3 in long.
particulars.note: Read in a tertiary source only.

particulars.title: Bilge keels
particulars.summary: About 300 ft long and 25 in deep, amidships.
particulars.note: Report, Structure.

sheer.note: D and E decks stand 13 ft higher above the waterline at the bow and 5 ft higher at the stern than at their lowest point amidships. The transcription gives an inconsistent figure for F deck at the bow, read here as a transcription error.

decks.name: Boat deck
decks.note: About 500 ft long with its fore end 190 ft from the bow (report); positions are converted to the forward perpendicular by subtracting the stem overhang.

decks.name: A deck (Promenade)
decks.note: About 500 ft long (report), assumed to share the extent of the Boat deck; 9 ft 6 in below it. Wikipedia gives 546 ft for the A-deck superstructure.

decks.name: B deck (Bridge)
decks.note: Level shared by the forecastle (125 ft), the 550 ft midship superstructure and the poop (about 105 ft), separated by two well decks of about 50 ft. 9 ft below A deck.

decks.name: C deck (Shelter)
decks.note: Runs the whole length of the ship and is exposed in the two well decks; 9 ft below B deck. The height above keel adds the load draught to the report's height above the waterline.

decks.name: D deck (Saloon)
decks.note: 20 ft above the load waterline amidships, 33 ft at the bow and 25 ft at the stern.

decks.name: E deck (Upper)
decks.note: 11 ft above the load waterline amidships. Bulkheads C to J are watertight up to this deck.

decks.name: F deck (Middle)
decks.note: 2 ft 6 in above the load waterline amidships.

decks.name: G deck (Lower)
decks.note: 5 ft 6 in below the load waterline amidships. Interrupted by the boiler and engine rooms: 190 ft forward of the boilers and 210 ft aft of the machinery.

decks.name: Orlop deck
decks.note: 13 ft 6 in below the load waterline; interrupted like G deck. The mail-room floor in No. 3 hold was 24 ft above the keel.

decks.name: Tank top (inner bottom)
decks.note: The double bottom is 63 in deep on the centre line (78 in under the reciprocating engines) and runs from bulkhead A to 20 ft before bulkhead P.

bulkheads.note: Built to C deck, watertight to D deck. Position is the running sum of the compartment lengths given by the report; bulkheads were stepped in places, so stations are nominal.
Running sum of compartment lengths. Forward bulkhead of the boiler rooms.
Running sum of compartment lengths. Between boiler rooms 6 and 5; the damage ended about 2 ft abaft it.
Running sum of compartment lengths: 89 ft abaft amidships, against "90 ft abaft amidships" in the report.

compartments.name: Forepeak
compartments.note: 46 ft long; peak tank below, store rooms above.

compartments.name: No. 3 hold
compartments.note: 51 ft long; mail and baggage rooms on the Orlop deck, squash court on G deck.

compartments.name: No. 5 boiler room
compartments.note: 57 ft long; five double-ended boilers. Opened in the forward starboard bunker, about 2 ft abaft bulkhead E.

compartments.name: No. 4 boiler room
compartments.note: 57 ft long; five double-ended boilers. The report judged damage here "very doubtful"; water later rose through the stokehold plates.

compartments.name: Turbine engine room
compartments.note: 57 ft long. The two emergency dynamos stood on a platform in its casing at saloon-deck level.

compartments.name: Electric engine room
compartments.note: 63 ft long; the four main 400 kW dynamos.

compartments.name: After peak
compartments.note: 36 ft long; trimming tank below, stores above.

funnels.note: Station derived from the report's statement that the uptakes united immediately above the bulkhead between two boiler rooms (here bulkhead E). Top at 175 ft above keel (Wikipedia); elliptical section 24 ft 6 in by 19 ft and rake of 2 in per foot from secondary sources. The height of the base above the deckhouse is the project's estimate. Other heights circulate, such as 163 ft 8 in attributed to the builder's rigging plan, which could not be traced to a page read.
Station derived from bulkhead G, between boiler rooms 4 and 3. Dimensions as for the first funnel.
Station derived from bulkhead J, between boiler rooms 2 and 1. Dimensions as for the first funnel.

A ventilator over the turbine room carrying the galley flues, not a boiler uptake (report). Station obtained by keeping the 117 ft spacing of the others; Halpern places the fourth funnel at about 578 to 590 ft aft of the forward perpendicular.

masts.note: A steel pole mast with a teak top, standing within the forecastle and carrying the crow's nest (report). The exact station was not found in the sources read; it is placed by the project near the after end of the forecastle. Masthead height and rake are commonly quoted figures not verified in a primary source.
Abaft the fourth funnel (Wilding, as quoted by Halpern). The exact station was not found in the sources read; it is placed by the project near the after end of the Boat deck.

zones.name: Forecastle deck
zones.note: 125 ft long, at the level of B deck.

zones.name: Forward well deck
zones.note: About 50 ft of C deck open to the sky between the forecastle and the superstructure.

zones.name: After well deck
zones.note: About 50 ft of C deck open to the sky between the superstructure and the poop.

zones.name: Poop deck
zones.note: About 105 ft long, at the level of B deck, carrying the docking bridge.

zones.name: Navigating bridge and wheelhouse
zones.note: At the fore end of the Boat deck, 190 ft from the bow (report); the fore-and-aft extent is the project's estimate.

zones.name: Officers' quarters
zones.note: Deckhouse around the wheelhouse and the forward funnel casing, with the Marconi rooms abaft that casing (report); extent estimated by the project. Collapsibles A and B were stowed on its roof.

zones.name: Enclosed forward promenade of A deck
zones.note: A glazed screen 192 ft long at the forward end of A deck on both sides.

zones.name: Forward expansion joint
zones.note: The report states that the Boat and A decks had two expansion joints. Their stations were not found in the sources read; this one is placed by the project abaft the first funnel.

zones.name: After expansion joint
zones.note: Lookout Symons saw the ship part abaft the after expansion plate, about abeam the after funnel or a little forward of it (as quoted by Halpern). Station placed by the project accordingly.
